svg.title: Temporary flight restrictions (TFRs)
svg.desc: Plan view of two common TFRs. A presidential or VIP TFR has a 10 nautical mile inner core and a 30 nautical mile outer ring, surface up to but not including FL 180; in the outer ring VFR flight needs a flight plan, transponder code and two-way radio contact. A sporting event TFR covers a 3 nautical mile radius up to and including 3,000 feet AGL from one hour before to one hour after the event. TFRs are published by NOTAM and are not on the sectional chart.
svg.text: Published by NOTAM, not printed on the sectional. Check before every flight, and again close to departure.
Surface up to, not incl., FL 180.
Inner core 10 NM: closed to most
flights. Outer ring 30 NM: VFR needs a
flight plan, a discrete transponder code
and two-way radio contact with ATC.
3 NM radius, up to and including
3,000 ft AGL, from 1 hour before to
Fires, floods, relief work: stay clear
so rescue and fire aircraft can work.
Get a briefing (91.103); it includes TFRs. Re-check close to departure, because TFRs change.
Do not enter unless the NOTAM allows it: intercepts, fines and certificate action can follow.
Check tfr.faa.gov or Flight Service. Source: 14 CFR 91.103, 91.137, 91.141; 14 CFR 99.7; AIM 3-5-3.
